title: Bearings and Midpoints
kicker: Cambridge Lower Secondary · Mathematics 0862 · Stage 8 · Geometry and Measure
summary: Read, measure, draw and calculate three-figure bearings (including back bearings), and use coordinates to find the midpoint of a line segment.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Understand bearings as a way of giving a direction, and use them: read, measure, draw and calculate bearings. [8Gp.01]
Use coordinates to find the midpoint of a line segment. [8Gp.02]

blocks.text: Pilots, sailors and map readers need a precise way to say which direction to travel. 'North-east' is not exact enough — a **bearing** gives the direction as an angle. In the second part of the page you will use coordinates to find the exact middle of a line segment, its **midpoint**, without drawing anything.
1. Key words

items: bearing
الاتجاه بالزاوية (الاتجاه الملاحي) — an angle measured clockwise from North, written with 3 figures
North line
خط الشمال — a vertical line pointing North drawn at the starting point
clockwise
في اتجاه عقارب الساعة — the direction the hands of a clock turn
three-figure bearing
اتجاه بثلاثة أرقام — e.g. 045°, 120°, 300°
back bearing
الاتجاه العكسي — the bearing for the return journey
scale drawing
رسم بمقياس رسم — an accurate drawing with all lengths reduced in the same ratio
coordinates
الإحداثيات — (x, y): across first, then up or down
line segment
قطعة مستقيمة — the part of a line between two end points
midpoint
نقطة المنتصف — the point exactly halfway between two points

blocks.text: 2. What is a bearing?
A bearing follows **three rules**:

items: It is measured **from North**.
It is measured **clockwise**.
It is written with **three figures** (add zeros in front if needed): 5° is written 005°, 45° is written 045°.

blocks.title: قواعد الـ bearing
items: ابدأ دايماً من الشمال (N).
لف مع عقارب الساعة.
اكتب الزاوية بـ 3 أرقام: 45° تتكتب 045°.
«bearing of B from A» يعني ارسم خط الشمال عند A (النقطة اللي بعد كلمة from).

blocks.text: 3. Measuring and drawing bearings
'The bearing of B **from** A' means: stand at **A**, face North, and turn clockwise until you face B. So the North line and the protractor go at the point after the word **from**.

items: Draw (or find) the North line at the starting point.
Join the starting point to the other point.
Measure the angle **clockwise** from the North line to this line.
If the angle is more than 180°, it is easier to measure the anticlockwise angle from North and subtract it from 360°.
Write the answer with three figures.

blocks.text: **Drawing a bearing**: to draw a path on a bearing of 130° from P, draw a North line at P, put the protractor's centre on P with 0° on the North line, mark 130° going clockwise, and draw the line. For a bearing such as 250°, you can mark 180° (South) and then another 70° clockwise, or measure 360° − 250° = 110° anticlockwise from North.

**Bearings and scale drawings**: in a journey question, a bearing gives the direction and a scale gives the distance. Example: a boat sails 6 km on a bearing of 060°, using a scale of 1 cm to 1 km. Draw a North line, measure 60° clockwise, and mark a point 6 cm along the line.
4. Back bearings (the return journey)

If you know the bearing of B from A, you can work out the bearing of A from B without measuring. The two North lines are **parallel**, so the angle facts from the parallel-lines topic apply. The direction from B back to A is exactly opposite (a half turn, 180°) to the direction from A to B.

blocks.caption: The bearing of B from A is 070°. The two North lines are parallel, so the angle at B between South and BA is also 70° (alternate angles). The bearing of A from B is 180° + 70° = 250°.

items: If the bearing is **less than 180°**: back bearing = bearing **+ 180°**. (070° → 250°)
If the bearing is **more than 180°**: back bearing = bearing **− 180°**. (300° → 120°)
Check: the two bearings always differ by exactly 180°.

blocks.text: 5. The midpoint of a line segment
The midpoint is halfway along the line segment, so it is halfway across **and** halfway up. Halfway between two numbers is their mean (add and divide by 2). So:

blocks.title: Midpoint rule
blocks.text: The midpoint of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is ( (x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2 , (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2 ). Add the x-coordinates and halve; add the y-coordinates and halve.

blocks.text: **Working backwards**: if you know one end A and the midpoint M, the other end B is the same step again from M. Step from A to M, then repeat it. As a rule: B = (2 × M's x − A's x, 2 × M's y − A's y).

blocks.title: نقطة المنتصف
blocks.text: اجمع الـ x واقسم على 2، واجمع الـ y واقسم على 2. خلي بالك من الإشارات السالبة: (−3 + 5) ÷ 2 = 1. ولو عندك طرف ونقطة المنتصف: كرّر نفس الخطوة من المنتصف علشان توصل للطرف التاني.
6. Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — The angle measured clockwise from North at A to the line AB is 72°. Write the bearing of B from A. Then write the bearing of a point C that is due South-West of A. [2]

items: Bearing of B from A = **072°** (three figures).
South-West is halfway between South (180°) and West (270°): **225°**.

blocks.text: **Worked example 2** — From a lighthouse L, a ship S is 50° anticlockwise from North. Work out the bearing of S from L. [1]

items: Bearings are clockwise: 360° − 50° = **310°**.

blocks.text: Common mistake: writing 050°. That would be 50° clockwise — on the other side of the North line.
**Worked example 3** — (a) The bearing of B from A is 065°. Work out the bearing of A from B. (b) The bearing of D from C is 300°. Work out the bearing of C from D. [2]

items: (b) 300° is more than 180°, so subtract 180°: **120°**.

blocks.text: **Worked example 4** — A boat leaves harbour H and sails 5 km on a bearing of 120°. Use a scale of 1 cm to 1 km to show its position. [2]

items: Mark H and draw a North line through it.
Put the protractor centre on H, 0° on the North line, and mark 120° clockwise (this is 30° past East).
Draw a line from H through the mark and measure **5 cm** along it (5 km at 1 cm to 1 km). Mark the boat B.
Check: the bearing of H from B should be 120° + 180° = 300°.

blocks.text: **Worked example 5** — Find the midpoint of A(−2, 7) and B(6, −1). [2]

items: Midpoint = **(2, 3)**.

blocks.text: Common mistake: subtracting instead of adding, (6 − (−2)) ÷ 2 = 4. That is half the distance across, not the midpoint.
**Worked example 6** — M(3, −1) is the midpoint of AB. A is the point (−1, 4). Find the coordinates of B. [2]

items: From A to M: x goes from −1 to 3 (+4); y goes from 4 to −1 (−5).
Do the same step again from M: x = 3 + 4 = 7; y = −1 − 5 = −6.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Measuring anticlockwise, or measuring from East or from the line AB instead of from North.
Putting the North line at the wrong point: 'bearing of B from A' — the North line goes at A.
Writing only two figures: 45° instead of 045°.
For back bearings, adding 180° to a bearing that is already more than 180° (giving more than 360°).
Midpoint: subtracting the coordinates, or forgetting to halve.
Sign errors with negative coordinates: −3 + 5 = 2, not −8.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: 'Measure the bearing of B from A.' — draw the North line if it is missing, measure clockwise, give three figures. Measure carefully to the nearest degree.
'The bearing of P from Q is 070°. Work out the bearing of Q from P.' — no measuring needed: ±180°.
A map with a scale: find the real distance and the bearing, or plot a point from a bearing and a distance.
'Work out the coordinates of the midpoint of AB.' — answer as (x, y) with brackets and a comma.
'M is the midpoint of AB… find the coordinates of B.' — work backwards with the same step.
Explain/critique: spot a mistake in someone's bearing or midpoint method and correct it.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Bearings and Midpoints — practice
blocks.intro: 15 questions. Type bearings as three figures (e.g. 045) and coordinates as (x, y). Diagrams marked NOT TO SCALE must be worked out, not measured.

questions.q: What is the three-figure bearing of due West?
questions.e: West is three quarter turns clockwise from North: 3 × 90° = 270°.

questions.q: Write the bearing of South-West as a three-figure bearing.
questions.e: South is 180°, West is 270°; South-West is halfway: 225°.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT written correctly as a bearing?
questions.e: Bearings are always written with three figures. 45° must be written 045°.

questions.q: Q is 35° anticlockwise from North at P. Write the bearing of Q from P.
questions.e: Bearings are measured clockwise from North: 360° − 35° = 325°.

questions.q: The angle between South and the line PQ is 40°, as shown. Write the bearing of Q from P.
questions.e: South is 180°. Q is 40° before South going clockwise (on the East side), so the bearing is 180° − 40° = 140°.

questions.q: The bearing of B from A is 065°. Work out the bearing of A from B.
The bearing of T from S is 300°. Work out the bearing of S from T.
Find the midpoint of A(2, 3) and B(8, 7).
Find the midpoint of P(−4, 6) and Q(2, −2).
questions.e: x: (−4 + 2) ÷ 2 = −2 ÷ 2 = −1; y: (6 + (−2)) ÷ 2 = 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Midpoint (−1, 2). (1 mark for one coordinate correct.)

questions.q: Find the midpoint of C(1, 4) and D(4, 9).
questions.e: x: (1 + 4) ÷ 2 = 2.5; y: (4 + 9) ÷ 2 = 6.5. Midpoint (2.5, 6.5). A midpoint does not have to be on whole numbers.

questions.q: Omar says the midpoint of (2, 6) and (8, 10) is (3, 2) because 8 − 2 = 6 and 10 − 6 = 4, then he halved. What is the correct midpoint?
questions.e: Add, do not subtract: ((2 + 8) ÷ 2, (6 + 10) ÷ 2) = (5, 8). Omar found half the distance across and up, not the midpoint.

questions.q: M(4, 5) is the midpoint of AB. A is the point (1, 2). Find the coordinates of B.
M(1, 2) is the midpoint of CD. C is the point (−3, 5). Work out the y-coordinate of D.
questions.e: From C to M, y goes from 5 to 2 (−3). Repeat from M: 2 − 3 = −1. (The x-coordinate: −3 to 1 is +4, so x = 5; D = (5, −1).)

questions.q: Explain why the bearing of A from B is always 180° different from the bearing of B from A.
questions.ms: 1 mark: the North lines at A and B are parallel. 1 mark: so the angles are linked by alternate/co-interior angles (or: the return direction is a half turn), giving a difference of 180°. Accept a correct explanation with a labelled sketch.
questions.e: The North lines at A and B are parallel. Going from B back to A is the opposite direction, a half turn. Using the parallel North lines, the angle from South at B to BA equals the angle from North at A to AB (alternate angles), so the bearing at B is 180° plus (or minus) the bearing at A.

questions.q: A boat sails 5 km from port P on a bearing of 120°. Using a scale of 1 cm to 1 km, make an accurate drawing to show the position of the boat B.
questions.ms: 1 mark: North line drawn at P and the line PB at 120° clockwise from North (±2°). 1 mark: PB = 5 cm (±2 mm), B labelled.
questions.e: Draw a North line at P. With the protractor centre on P and 0° on the North line, mark 120° clockwise (30° past East). Draw the line and mark B at 5 cm from P.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Bearings: from North, clockwise, three figures (045°, not 45°).
'Bearing of B from A' — the North line and protractor go at A.
Back bearing: add 180° if the bearing is less than 180°, subtract 180° if it is more.
Midpoint of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) = ((x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2, (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2).
To find an end point from the midpoint, repeat the step from the known end to the midpoint.
